lines.en: 10. The one who takes to bed will rise quickly.
[11 is missing].
12. The one who takes to bed will be sick for a short time.
13. The one who takes to bed will be sick for a long time.

lines.text: ιδ'. <Ὁ κατακλιθεὶς> μετέλθῃ τοῦ τόπου καὶ ὑγιαίνει.
lines.en: 14. <The one who takes to bed> should change place and he will be healthy.
15. The one who takes to bed will die.

lines.text: ις'. <Ὁ κατακλιθεὶς> μετέλθῃ τοῦ τόπου καὶ ὑγιαίνει.
lines.en: 16. <The one who takes to bed> should change place and he will be healthy.
17. The one who takes to bed will be sick for a long time.

lines.text: ιη'. <Ὁ κατακλιθεὶς> μετέλθῃ τοῦ τόπου καὶ ὑγιαίνει.
lines.en: 18. <The one who takes to bed> should change place and he will be healthy.

lines.text: ιθ'. <Ὁ κατακλιθεὶς> ἀπὸ ἰατρῶν ἐπιμελείας ζήσεται.
lines.en: 19. <The one who takes to bed> will live by the care of doctors.
20. The one who takes to bed will not die.
21. The one who takes to bed will be in danger.
22. The one who takes to bed will not die.
23. The one who takes to bed will be sick for a long time.
24. The one who takes to bed will be sick for a long time.

lines.text: κε'. <Ὁ κατακλιθεὶς>, ἐὰν παρέλθῃ τὰς γ' ἡμέρας, ζήσεται.
lines.en: 25. <The one who takes to bed>, if he passes the 3 days, will live.
26. <The one who takes to bed> having been sick for a short time will die.
27. <The one who takes to bed> will not be very sick.

lines.text: κη'. <Ὁ κατακλιθεὶς> μετελθὼν τοῦ τόπου ζῇ.
lines.en: 28. <The one who takes to bed> having changed place will live.
29. <The one who takes to bed> will live by the care of <doctors?>.

lines.text: λ'. <Ὁ κατακλιθεὶς> κἂν τρώγῃ κἂν μὴ τρώγῃ ζήσει.
lines.en: 30. <The one who takes to bed> whether he eats or does not eat will live.

lines.text: Τῆς σελήνης αἱ ἡμέραι αἱ μέν εἰσι πεφωτισμέναι, αἱ δὲ ἀφώτιστοι·
lines.en: Of the moon, some days are illuminated, and some are unilluminated;

lines.text: καὶ αἱ ἔχουσαι τὰ φῶτα εἰσὶν αὗται· α'· β'· γ'· ζ'· θ'· ι'· ια'· ιγ'· ιδ'· ις'·
lines.en: and those having the lights are these: 1, 2, 3, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16,

lines.text: ιζ'· ιθ'· κ'· κβ'· κγ'· κς'· κη'· λ'· αἱ δὲ ἀφώτιστοι αὗται· δ'· ε'· ς'· η'·
lines.en: 17, 19, 20, 22, 23, 26, 28, 30; and the unilluminated are these: 4, 5, 6, 8,

lines.text: ιβ'· ιε'· ιη'· κα'· κδ'· κε'· κζ'· κθ'. ἐὰν οὖν κατακλιθῇ τις ἐν φῶς ἐχούσῃ
lines.en: 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 25, 27, 29. If therefore someone takes to bed on a day having light,

lines.text: ἡμέρᾳ, σωθήσεται καὶ ταχέως ἐγερθήσεται· ἐὰν δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἀφωτίστοις,
lines.en: he will be saved and will rise quickly; but if on the unilluminated ones,

lines.text: τεθνήξεται. ὁμοίως θεωρεῖται καὶ ἐπὶ παιδίῳ γεννωμένῳ· τὰ γεννώμενα
lines.en: he will die. Similarly it is considered also for a child being born: those born

lines.text: ἐν ταῖς ἐχούσαις φῶς ἐπίσημα καὶ εὐτυχῆ· τὰ δὲ γεννώμενα ἐν ταῖς
lines.en: on those having light are notable and fortunate; but those born on the
unilluminated ones are unfortunate and poor.

sections.en: 3 the codex has ὀλίγων ('few'). 5, 7 and 9 the codex has Μετέλθει ('he will pursue'). 10 the codex has ἰατρὸν ('doctor'). 11 the codex has ἀποθνήσκῃ ('he may die') (and thus below). 12 the codex has κινδυνεύσῃ ('he may be in danger'). 19 the codex has τὸν τόπον ('the place'), compare above lines 5, 7 and 9. 21 the codex has τρόγει ('he eats'). 27 the codex has τεθνήξαται ('he will die'). 29 the codex has αὐτυχῆ ('unfortunate').

summary.headline: The Moon’s Illuminated Days
summary.text: Astrological doctrine of the Moon’s illuminated and unilluminated days: those saved and rising quickly on illuminated days, while those born then are notable and fortunate; births on unilluminated days bring death, misfortune, and poverty.
